headline: Flood alert: Saturday's HSC exams postponed under Chattogram Board
summary: Exams in Chattogram, Cox's Bazar, Rangamati, Bandarban, and Khagrachhari districts are cancelled due to severe weather and flooding.
details: The Chattogram Education Board has postponed the Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) exams scheduled for Saturday, July 11, across five districts: Chattogram, Cox's Bazar, Rangamati, Bandarban, and Khagrachhari.
The decision was confirmed by Controller of Examinations Parvez Sajjad Chowdhury, who stated that the adverse weather conditions and flood situations have made it impossible to conduct the exams.
The postponed exam is for the Information and Communication Technology (ICT) subject. This follows a previous postponement of the exam scheduled for July 8.
The region has been devastated by heavy rainfall, leading to widespread flooding and landslides. Reports indicate that 29 people have been killed in these disasters.
Students in the districts affected by the flood are advised to stay updated on the new dates for the rescheduled exams.
caption:
Severe flooding and landslides have forced the postponement of HSC exams in five districts under the Chattogram Board.

The Chattogram Education Board has postponed the Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) exams scheduled for Saturday, July 11, across five districts: Chattogram, Cox's Bazar, Rangamati, Bandarban, and Khagrachhari.

The decision was confirmed by Controller of Examinations Parvez Sajjad Chowdhury, who stated that the adverse weather conditions and flood situations have made it impossible to conduct the exams.

The postponed exam is for the Information and Communication Technology (ICT) subject. This follows a previous postponement of the exam scheduled for July 8.

The region has been devastated by heavy rainfall, leading to widespread flooding and landslides. Reports indicate that 29 people have been killed in these disasters.

Students in the districts affected by the flood are advised to stay updated on the new dates for the rescheduled exams.

#Bangladesh #Chattogram #HSC2024 #FloodAlert #EducationNews

Source: Prothom Alo, Dhaka Tribune, Somoy News, Jamuna TV, The Daily Star

headline: BMD warns of heavy to very heavy rain across 8 divisions
summary: The Bangladesh Meteorological Department forecasts significant rainfall, warning of potential landslides in hilly areas and waterlogging in major cities.
details: The Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD) has issued a warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall across all eight divisions of the country over the next 24 hours.
According to meteorologist Dr. Md. Omar Faruq, the active monsoon will bring rainfall ranging from 44 to 88 mm (heavy) and exceeding 88 mm (very heavy) in various areas.
The BMD warns that this intense rainfall may lead to temporary waterlogging in the low-lying areas of Dhaka and Chattogram cities.
Additionally, there is a significant risk of landslides in the hilly regions of the Chattogram division due to the heavy downpour.
Residents in the affected areas are advised to take necessary precautions and avoid unnecessary travel to the hilly regions.
caption:
Heavy to very heavy rain is forecast for all 8 divisions of Bangladesh. Be cautious of landslides and waterlogging!

The Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD) has issued a warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall across all eight divisions of the country over the next 24 hours.

According to meteorologist Dr. Md. Omar Faruq, the active monsoon will bring rainfall ranging from 44 to 88 mm (heavy) and exceeding 88 mm (very heavy) in various areas.

The BMD warns that this intense rainfall may lead to temporary waterlogging in the low-lying areas of Dhaka and Chattogram cities.

Additionally, there is a significant risk of landslides in the hilly regions of the Chattogram division due to the heavy downpour.

Residents in the affected areas are advised to take necessary precautions and avoid unnecessary travel to the hilly regions.
